# 02. Brand Strategy

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Ensure the site expresses a coherent, credible, differentiated brand without relying on inaccessible or unmaintainable decoration.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A brand positioning statement with audience, category, promise, proof, and point of difference.
- [ ] A tone-of-voice standard with approved vocabulary, banned phrases, reading level, and examples for headings, CTAs, errors, and microcopy.
- [ ] A brand proof library containing credentials, outcomes, case studies, testimonials, logos, awards, media mentions, certifications, and process evidence.
- [ ] A visual identity reference covering logo use, color roles, typography, spacing attitude, icon style, photography direction, and motion restraint.
- [ ] A trust standard that defines which claims require evidence, citations, dates, screenshots, metrics, or client approval.
- [ ] A competitor differentiation note explaining what the site must not look or sound like.
- [ ] A brand governance rule for who can approve public claims, imagery, testimonials, and regulated wording.
- [ ] A fallback plan for missing brand assets using open-source fonts, owned photography, client-provided images, or permissively licensed media.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The brand must be recognizable from the first viewport without depending only on a tiny logo in navigation.
- [ ] The voice must fit the business model: premium service sites must be clear and confident, not inflated or evasive.
- [ ] Brand claims must be specific, verifiable, and proportional to the available proof.
- [ ] Color, typography, imagery, and motion must improve comprehension and trust rather than only decorate.
- [ ] A local business brand must align website name, address, phone, categories, and services with public listings.
- [ ] A portfolio brand must show the work, role, constraints, outcomes, and taste level quickly.
- [ ] A multilingual brand must preserve meaning and trust in each locale rather than translating slogans literally.
- [ ] The brand system must remain usable in plain HTML/CSS without proprietary design system runtime dependencies.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check that every public claim has an approved source or evidence owner.
- [ ] Check that the homepage, about page, service pages, case studies, and contact page use the same positioning logic.
- [ ] Check that all testimonials have permission, attribution rules, and no misleading edits.
- [ ] Check that logo files include accessible alternatives and high-resolution formats where appropriate.
- [ ] Check that selected fonts are free for commercial use and can be self-hosted when privacy or performance requires it.
- [ ] Check that brand colors pass contrast requirements in actual UI states, not only in palette swatches.
- [ ] Check that imagery represents the real service, product, person, place, or audience where inspection matters.
- [ ] Check that AI-generated or stock imagery is not used in a way that misrepresents real capability, location, people, or results.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid generic premium cues such as vague luxury language, dark gradients, abstract shapes, and inflated claims without proof.
- [ ] Avoid brand systems that depend on inaccessible color-only distinctions.
- [ ] Avoid inconsistent names, abbreviations, phone formats, service names, or location labels.
- [ ] Avoid fake client logos, fake reviews, unverifiable numbers, or implied endorsements.
- [ ] Avoid using copyrighted imagery, fonts, icons, or copied competitor copy without rights.
- [ ] Avoid brand voice that hides practical information users need to decide.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The site must make the brand feel intentional at every touchpoint: navigation, headings, proof, forms, empty states, errors, and legal pages.
- [ ] Distinctiveness must come from positioning and execution quality, not noisy decoration.
- [ ] The identity must scale from homepage to small components without losing clarity.
- [ ] Brand assets must be organized so another developer can extend the site without guessing.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use asset audits to flag missing alt text, oversized logos, non-self-hosted fonts, and inconsistent image formats.
- [ ] Use metadata audits to confirm brand name consistency across titles, Open Graph tags, schema, manifest, and footer.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Brand positioning, promise, personality, tone, visual direction, trust signals, differentiators, vocabulary, and avoid-list are documented.
- [ ] The brand is recognizable in the first viewport through real product, service, place, person, work, or offer signals, not only nav text.
- [ ] Tone matches the audience, industry, price point, and trust needs without empty hype, unsupported claims, desperation, or generic marketing cliches.
- [ ] Visual brand direction covers color, typography, imagery, icon style, motion, spacing, layout, button style, section style, and overall mood.
- [ ] Credibility is supported by legitimate testimonials, case studies, client logos, credentials, certifications, partner links, photos, process proof, or metrics.
- [ ] Brand claims are accurate, permission-safe, non-confidential, non-deceptive, and reviewed for industry-specific risk where needed.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
